title: Fine-tuning versus prompt engineering: cost and when to use each

videos.script: A model gives the wrong kind of answer, and somebody says the word fine-tuning. {{word}} It sounds like the serious fix. Train the model on your own data, and the problem goes away. {{serious}} Sometimes it does. More often, a clearer prompt would have done the same job in an afternoon. {{afternoon}} The difference is where the change lands. A prompt changes what you send. Fine-tuning changes the weights. {{lands}} In this lesson you put the two side by side. What each one is good at, and what each one cannot fix. {{side}} Then you count the cost. Collecting examples, training, testing, hosting, and doing it all again when the base model changes. {{cost}} You will leave with a ladder of four steps, and a rule for which rung to stand on. {{ladder}}
